laws.summary: GrassEye must expand only through the single-line mediator to job-flow to ability-group architecture.
forbidden: Second orchestration layer.
Universal agent runtime.
Parallel planner.
NerveBus or central dispatcher resurrection.
New active architecture outside mediator -> flow -> ability group -> child ability.

laws.summary: The mediator may route user demands to job flows but must not execute business steps or browser actions.
forbidden: Mediator directly calling browser click/fill/upload primitives.
Mediator containing Amazon-specific or Facebook-specific step logic.
Mediator becoming a workflow engine.
Mediator storing business process state.

laws.summary: Each new user demand must be implemented as one explicit job flow under src/plugins/<job-id>.
forbidden: One flow owning multiple unrelated jobs.
Job flow creating generic orchestration.
Business logic placed inside ability groups.
Flow importing private runtime internals from other jobs.
Flow importing unrelated job flow code.
Flow importing non-facade capability files.
Top-level files directly under src/plugins pretending to be shared job routers.

laws.summary: Ability groups must own same-kind reusable actions and must not contain business-specific workflow logic.
forbidden: Amazon-specific workflow inside an ability group.
Facebook-specific workflow inside an ability group.
Ability group importing job flow files.
Ability group importing unrelated capability owner files.
Ability group deciding business success.
Ability group dispatching multiple unrelated action kinds.

laws.summary: Each child ability must perform one atomic action and must not contain multi-step business workflow.
forbidden: Child ability performing a full business flow.
Child ability calling unrelated ability groups.
Child ability importing unrelated capability owner files.
Child ability making business decisions.
Child ability containing hidden orchestration.

laws.summary: New active directories must belong to the approved architecture root allowlist.
forbidden: New active top-level source folders outside the architecture allowlist.
Ad-hoc folders for experiments.
Unowned helper folders.
Temporary architecture roots.

laws.summary: Shared infrastructure under src/lib must remain infrastructure-only and must not absorb business flow or ability logic.
forbidden: Business job flow inside src/lib.
Ability group implementation inside src/lib.
Generic service layer hiding business workflow.
Shared helper created before two real call sites exist.

laws.summary: Every new user demand must enter through a job schema, mediator route, explicit flow, and acceptance proof.
forbidden: New demand without job schema.
New demand without mediator route.
New demand without explicit flow.
New demand without acceptance smoke.
New demand hidden inside existing unrelated flow.

laws.summary: AI may only serve bounded choice judging and must not become a workflow planner or next-action controller.
forbidden: AI outputting nextAction.
AI outputting actionPlan.
AI outputting browser command.
AI outputting selector or coordinate.
AI deciding final sensitive actions.
AI generating workflow steps at runtime.

laws.summary: Any new architecture layer, source root, job category, or ability group family must update architecture law before code is accepted.
forbidden: Code-first architecture change.
Unapproved new root folder.
Unapproved new layer.
Silent architectural expansion.

laws.summary: The audit system must keep one real execution chain from laws to manifests to generated artifacts to runner.
forbidden: Manual enforcement matrix truth.
ci:full bypassing codex:entry-gate.
Runner-owned law binding truth.
Parallel audit truth chains.

laws.summary: Each active audit law must remain structurally parseable from the law file with stable metadata.
forbidden: Unstructured active laws that cannot be parsed stably.
Hard-binding inspector filenames inside the law body.
One law spanning multiple capability domains.

laws.summary: Each capabilityDomain must have one owner inspector and one manifest-owned execution authority.
forbidden: One script carrying multiple capability domains.
Multiple owner inspectors for one capability domain.
Helper or wrapper paths pretending to be owner inspectors.

laws.summary: The law registry, enforcement matrix, audit plan, and conflict snapshots must be generated artifacts.
forbidden: Manual editing of generated audit artifacts.
Runner consumption of legacy manual matrix files.
CI skipping artifact regeneration.

laws.summary: The runner is an executor only and must not own law truth, ordering truth, or binding truth.
forbidden: Runner-maintained manual script ordering truth.
Runner-maintained law to inspector mapping.
Runner interpreting business laws directly.

laws.summary: Inspector evidence must remain consistent with the declared evidenceMode and cannot fake AST or hybrid enforcement.
forbidden: String search pretending to be AST primary judgment.
Blind delegate or hollow enforcement.
Blueprint or law drift hidden behind PASS results.

laws.summary: Law, blueprint, and inspector must form a closed authority chain whenever blueprint-backed enforcement is declared.
forbidden: Inspector claiming blueprint integration without reading blueprint anchors.
PASS results when law or blueprint anchors are missing.
Blueprint-only or law-only enforcement claims.

laws.summary: The audit system must have a meta-inspection capability domain that can inspect the audit system itself.
forbidden: Dispersed patch scripts holding long-term system-level audit truth.
Generated-artifact drift with no meta inspector alarm.
Duplicate owner or fake enforcement escaping the audit-system gate.

laws.summary: Manual matrix truth, duplicate mappings, giant cross-domain inspectors, and retired enforcement remnants should converge toward deletion.
forbidden: Manual matrix truth surviving as runtime authority.
Parallel registry or mapping chains.
Generated and source files with overlapping authority.

laws.summary: Executable audit outputs must be binary PASS/FAIL results only and must not introduce warning-grade verdict tiers.
An ability group may exist only when it owns one same-kind reusable action family and has an active governing law.
forbidden: Ability group without active law.
Ability group created for one business job only.
Ability group owning multiple unrelated action kinds.
Business flow disguised as ability group.
Universal agent runtime disguised as ability group.

laws.summary: Each child ability must perform one atomic action and must not hide workflow logic.
forbidden: Child ability performing a full business flow.
Child ability deciding next business step.
Child ability calling unrelated ability groups.
Child ability importing job plugins.
Child ability hiding planner behavior.

laws.summary: Job flows may use ability groups only through public facades and must not import non-facade or private runtime internals.
forbidden: Plugin importing non-facade ability files.
Plugin importing ability runtime internals.
Plugin importing ability private child files.
Ability group importing unrelated capability owner files.
Ability group importing plugin files.
Facade re-exporting unrelated owners.
Barrel laundering of private imports.

laws.summary: Ability groups must stay business-neutral and must not contain platform-specific workflow logic.
forbidden: Amazon-specific workflow inside an ability group.
Facebook-specific workflow inside an ability group.
Order upload process order inside an ability group.
Product-video mining workflow inside an ability group.
Business final status inside an ability group.

laws.summary: Ability groups must not use AI as planner, next-action chooser, selector generator, or browser-command generator.
forbidden: AI returning nextAction.
AI returning actionPlan.
AI returning browserCommand.
AI returning selector or coordinate.
AI generating runtime workflow steps.

laws.summary: Ability groups may create action evidence refs but must not own separate evidence stores or private log systems.
forbidden: Private evidence database inside an ability group.
Private JSONL log system inside an ability group.
Forged evidence ref.
Stale evidence reused as fresh proof.
Sensitive data logged by an ability group.

laws.summary: Retired standalone ability owners must not return as active capability groups.
forbidden: nerve-bus active owner.
orchestration active owner.
geometry-guard active owner.
mouse-click active owner.
mouse-scroll active owner.
text-input active owner.
open active owner.
screenshot active owner.
video-download active owner.
universal-agent active owner.
planner active owner.

laws.summary: Capability group governance must be enforceable by audit before production readiness is claimed.
forbidden: Production readiness without capability-group audit.
Warning-only P0 capability-group finding.
Generated fake PASS.
Runner detached from active capability laws.
Manual generated artifact truth.

laws.summary: Active source files must remain owner-clear, role-clear, and small enough for safe Codex iteration.
Touched files must not get dirtier and must not cross hard purity limits.
Files must not mix incompatible GrassEye runtime roles.
Each job flow must own one business demand and must not become a generic workflow engine.
The mediator may route user demands but must not execute business steps or browser actions.
Ability groups must own same-kind reusable actions and must not absorb business workflow.
Child abilities must remain atomic and must not hide multi-step business workflow.
Type escapes must not bypass GrassEye contracts, schemas, or runtime safety.
Fake, mock, placeholder, no-op, demo, and fallback runtime paths must not survive in active source truth.
Bridge, compatibility, legacy, shadow, and dual-truth structures are forbidden unless an active law explicitly authorizes them.
Shared files must prove infrastructure ownership and must not become dumping grounds.
Evidence, logs, and result records must be truthful and must not be forged to satisfy acceptance.
Code-purity enforcement must be real, runner-visible, and unable to fake PASS.
Generated artifacts are evidence outputs, not hand-written source truth.
Code-purity enforcement should produce actionable inventories and split recommendations without pretending every inventory item is a P0 blocker.
Purity remediation must simplify the real structure, not hide the same mess behind another file.
Active source must not keep zombie files, zombie exports, orphan top-level declarations, or literal-dead code branches.
DOM Automation must remain business-neutral and must not contain platform-specific workflow logic.
forbidden: Amazon-specific workflow inside DOM Automation.
Facebook-specific workflow inside DOM Automation.
Business success decision inside DOM Automation.
DOM code importing src/plugins.
DOM code calling AI to plan browser actions.

laws.summary: Public consumers may import DOM Automation only through its public facade.
forbidden: Consumer importing src/capabilities/dom-automation/runtime.
Consumer importing DOM private contract internals.
Mediator importing any DOM runtime file.
App shell importing any DOM runtime file.

laws.summary: Expected DOM uncertainty must return structured statuses instead of escaping as ordinary exceptions.
forbidden: Locator not_found thrown as normal control flow.
Locator ambiguous thrown as normal control flow.
Fill/click/upload/verify returning success after unverified uncertainty.
Catch-and-swallow inside DOM runtime.

laws.summary: DOM snapshots must be privacy-safe structural summaries, not raw page dumps.
forbidden: Snapshot returning full HTML.
Snapshot returning cookies or storage.
Snapshot returning password values.
Snapshot returning full file input values.
Snapshot returning unbounded page text.

laws.summary: DOM location must use semantic signals and revalidation, not selector-only guesswork.
forbidden: Selector-only element identity.
CSS fallback marked as high confidence.
Ambiguous candidates returned as success.
Frame hint ignored when frame support is requested.
Business-specific selector hardcoding in DOM core.

laws.summary: Frame and shadow DOM handling must be explicit and must not pretend unsupported scopes are supported.
forbidden: Returning frameRef without action support.
Ignoring frameRef during fill/click/upload.
Pretending cross-origin frame contents were inspected.
Shadow DOM action without host-level revalidation.

laws.summary: DOM fill may write only caller-approved text into a revalidated writable element.
forbidden: Filling password inputs.
Filling empty or AI-generated business values.
Filling hidden or disabled elements.
Success without value verification.
Fill without before and after evidence.

laws.summary: DOM click must be located-element-first and must block sensitive irreversible actions.
forbidden: Coordinate-first click as DOM action identity.
Clicking hidden or disabled elements.
Sensitive irreversible click without review_required.
Click success without after evidence.
Expected text mismatch treated as success.

laws.summary: DOM upload may attach only a task-approved local file to a located file input.
forbidden: Arbitrary file path upload.
Upload target not located as file input.
Reading file content into AI or DOM snapshot.
Upload success without before and after evidence.
Business plugin directly using browser file-input private implementation.

laws.summary: DOM wait and verify must report observed page state, not business completion fiction.
forbidden: Unknown state returned as success.
File-selected state treated as final business success.
Login or captcha state downgraded to not_found.
Verification evidence ref that cannot be traced to an observed snapshot or action.
Business success terms hardcoded in DOM core.

laws.summary: DOM action evidence must be truthful while storage and logging ownership stay outside DOM Automation.
forbidden: DOM runtime owning evidence storage truth.
DOM runtime creating a private log system.
Forged screenshot or snapshot evidence.
Stale evidence reused as fresh proof.
Sensitive data logged from DOM snapshots or actions.

laws.summary: DOM Automation replaces retired standalone text input, mouse click, open, screenshot, and upload action owners for DOM page work.
forbidden: Standalone text-input ability owner resurrection.
Standalone mouse-click ability owner resurrection.
Coordinate-first page action owner resurrection.
Open/screenshot/upload standalone workflow owner resurrection.
Muscle-memory or platform registry as DOM workflow truth.

laws.summary: DOM scroll must bring a located element into viewport before any action and must not loop infinitely.
forbidden: Infinite scroll loop without a max-iteration budget.
Claiming element is in viewport without revalidation.
Scroll success without post-scroll visibility recheck.
Scrolling to an element that was not previously located.
Business plugin calling browser scroll primitive directly.

laws.summary: DOM option selection must handle native select and common custom dropdown patterns, verify the selection was applied, and return structured results.
forbidden: Selecting arbitrary option text not from caller-approved list.
Claiming selection success without verifying the displayed value changed.
Using fill to set a native select element's value directly.
Custom dropdown interaction without detecting its open/close state.
Multi-select without explicit caller approval of each selected value.

laws.summary: DOM overlay dismissal may only remove safe non-blocking consent or informational overlays and must return review_required for all ambiguous or sensitive dialogs.
forbidden: Dismissing authentication dialogs.
Dismissing business confirmation dialogs (e.g. payment, refund, deletion).
Dismissing overlays whose purpose cannot be determined from detectedState.
Clicking Escape as a universal dismiss without verifying overlay type.
Claiming dismiss success when the overlay is still present in the DOM.

laws.summary: DOM Automation must have runner-visible enforcement before production readiness can be claimed.
forbidden: Claiming DOM production readiness without DOM audit coverage.
DOM inspector detached from CI or audit plan.
Warning-only P0 DOM findings.
Acceptance smoke that uses fake success instead of real DOM actions.
Generated audit artifacts hand-edited to include DOM pass.

laws.summary: Facebook product video mining must remain one explicit plugin-owned flow that performs truthful probe, comment loading, video download, bounded AI judgment, reject-or-save, and persistence per round.
forbidden: Business loop logic outside src/plugins/facebook-product-video-mining.
Skipping download, AI judgment, or persistence while claiming saved products.
Mock, fixture, or placeholder success for real-platform mining.
Parallel second flow for the same Facebook mining demand.

laws.summary: Facebook product video mining must expose lawful start/status/latest routes through the local workbench and must keep acceptance and audit ownership wired into CI-FULL.
forbidden: App shell owning Facebook step order.
Missing mission start, run status, or latest status surface.
CI-FULL omitting Facebook mining acceptance after the domain is active.
Manifest pointing to a non-existent owner inspector.

laws.summary: The Facebook mining app-shell surface must ask the operator only for target product count and must derive all other mission parameters from governed defaults.
forbidden: Visible Facebook feed URL input in the workbench.
Visible Facebook provider selector in the workbench.
Visible Facebook model, max rounds, or max minutes fields in the workbench.
Client-side Facebook mission payload requiring feedEntryUrl, providerKind, modelName, maxRounds, or maxMinutes.
Facebook mission schema requiring operator-supplied parameters beyond targetProductCount.

laws.summary: Facebook mining must not default to mutating the operator's recommendation profile and must convert AI web-chat stalls into bounded review-required evidence instead of leaving runs indefinitely running.
forbidden: Default notInterestedEnabled=true for operator-facing Facebook mining.
AI web-chat judgment without a hard timeout.
AI web-chat timeout that leaves the run in running with no candidate evidence.
AI web-chat upload completion wait that can consume the whole judgment timeout.
Provider composer wait that ignores the task abort signal.
Typing a governed file path unless a provider file input is located.
Continuing web-chat upload, submit, or answer extraction after the active Chrome tab drifts away from the provider workspace.
Selecting an arbitrary existing provider tab when no saved Facebook workspace URL exists.
Matching old provider conversations by title text instead of pinning the opened workspace URL.

laws.summary: The Facebook mining workbench must expose saved product-seeding records for the active run and must provide a structured export for downstream senior-AI product selection.
forbidden: Workbench showing only run status while hiding saved PRODUCT_SEEDING records.
Exporting rejected, uncertain, failed, or review-required candidates as successful products.
Export payloads that omit source URL, product signals, AI reason, confidence, or artifact references.
Export logic outside the Facebook mining owner surface.

laws.summary: Facebook mining rounds must be controlled by a fixed flow state machine, fixed next-video action ladder, and multi-signal proof quorum; DOM selector feedback may observe but must not decide the next action.
forbidden: DOM next button candidates as the primary next-video decision source.
Single DOM signature change as the only proof of video transition.
next_video_did_not_change or next_video_not_confirmed stopping the whole mission.
Per-video download, comments, AI, duplicate, or navigation uncertainty treated as mission terminal.
AI returning workflow, selector, coordinate, browser command, or next action.

laws.summary: The root page must be a local workbench surface with health, mode, and lawful job flow entry points.
forbidden: Root page as endpoint documentation only.
Root page as marketing page.
Root page without health or mode visibility.
Root page without lawful job flow entry points.

laws.summary: Workbench input surfaces must collect structured inputs for explicit job flows and must not become a natural-language task planner.
forbidden: Natural-language universal task box.
AI generated action plan input.
Generic mission dashboard entry.
Single form mixing unrelated job flows.

laws.summary: The workbench must expose task status, failure reasons, and evidence references without replacing the evidence store.
forbidden: UI fabricating task success.
UI replacing evidence records.
UI hiding failureReason or review-required state.
Status panel pretending to be runtime logs or CI.

laws.summary: The local app shell must not resurrect universal dashboards, command consoles, visual runtime control panels, planners, or second orchestration.
forbidden: Universal mission dashboard.
Old commander console as active architecture.
Visual-runtime control panel.
AI next-action planner.
Browser or DOM action controller in the app shell.
src/lib/local-runtime importing plugin files outside plugin public facades.
src/lib/local-runtime importing ability files outside ability public facades.
App shell deciding business flow steps.

laws.summary: Runtime facts must enter the single Runtime Log Spine instead of console or private log channels.
Every runtime event must declare FLOW, DEBUG, or TRACE visibility and must not leak debug payload into FLOW.
Mission, run, round, step, capability, AI, and recovery events must carry trace context.
Any branch that changes execution direction must emit a structured runtime event before it returns, skips, retries, or throws.
Mandatory stages must emit paired started and terminal events with duration, reason, and failure details.
Large artifacts, DOM, AI raw output, and binary content must be referenced by refs and hashes instead of embedded inline.
All runtime sinks must redact secrets, storage data, signed URLs, and base64-like material before output.
Production mode must default to FLOW while DEBUG and TRACE remain explicit opt-in visibility levels.
DEBUG and TRACE logging must preserve enough evidence to explain one round down to single actions and retries.
Failed, skipped, and review-required events must carry classified failure metadata instead of free text alone.
All key terminal stage events must record duration and configured timeout evidence where applicable.
Each mission must produce a replayable debug bundle or emit structured bundle-write failure evidence.
AI request, upload, response, parse, and validation paths must emit provider proof, refs, hashes, and statuses.
Browser and DOM actions must log before state, attempted action, after state, duration, and failure class.
Every recovery and fallback path must emit a linked recovery trail tied to the originating failure.
Each plugin and capability must maintain a machine-enforced logging matrix for mandatory stages and contracts.
All runtime event types must come from the central event registry instead of free string literals.
CI must emit machine-readable and human-readable runtime log coverage reports with mandatory stage and failure coverage.
Any failed or review-required round must be diagnosable from runtime logs without rerunning the mission.
Automation, AI, DOM, browser, artifact, navigation, and recovery changes must satisfy log law before merge.
GrassEye startup must have exactly one user-facing startup command and one local startup entrypoint.
forbidden: Second user-facing startup command.
Startup entrypoint outside scripts/startup/launch-grasseye.mjs.
Startup acting as a general task launcher.

laws.summary: Startup may open the workbench but must not execute business flows, DOM abilities, browser actions, AI judgment, CI, or old registry readiness.
forbidden: Startup invoking a job flow.
Startup invoking DOM, browser, upload, click, fill, or evidence actions.
Startup invoking AI judgment or declaring provider readiness as mission truth.
Startup running CI or audit gates.
Startup requiring old registry readiness before app shell launch.

laws.summary: Startup readiness must be proven by the local app health endpoint, not by the home page or job-specific readiness.
forbidden: Readiness probe against the home page as the primary gate.
Readiness probe against a job-specific endpoint.
Readiness success without an HTTP status check.

laws.summary: Startup must emit structured terminal events with failure reasons while remaining subordinate to runtime logs and evidence.
forbidden: Unstructured startup failure output.
Startup logs replacing evidence or task status truth.
Startup logs exposing credentials, cookies, tokens, or provider secrets.
